title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed‑Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) measuring the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-produced intent→configuration artifacts under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" and a deterministic rule-based validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) we analyzed Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The validator flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation, with at most one permitted repair call per task) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0013888889; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0041666667]. Model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair). These artifact-grounded results are far below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, provider-call accounting, an explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this constrained regime, and reproducibility pointers to the canonical archived execution manifest in the evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and higher-order safety/policy constraints. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports recommend such workflow-centred mitigations but provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution. Motivated by this gap, we preregistered and executed a controlled paired study that reuses the exact same initial generated candidate for both conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics) so that any between-condition discordance can only arise from downstream guarded-stage processing (emulation observations or permitted repair). Our primary research question: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with full run accounting; (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation explaining a near-zero marginal effect in this regime; (4) prescriptive boundary conditions and reproducibility pointers into the canonical archived bundle.
sections.related_work: Surveys and architectural reports document the practical trend of combining LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise operational assurance for NetOps artifacts. These sources emphasize that correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional—syntactic parsing, command-ordering/workflow constraints, invariants (e.g., keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties may each require distinct V&V primitives. Tool-focused case studies show that mature static verifiers have expanded rule-sets and topology-aware checks but still miss some runtime-dependent behaviors, motivating emulator layering to exercise temporal behaviors and state transitions. Empirical prototypes integrating generation with verification report heterogeneous gains: in some regimes a verifier catches most dangerous errors, while in others emulation uncovers subtle runtime failures or environment-specific side effects. These prior findings motivated our paired design, which isolates guarded-stage contributions by holding generation constant across conditions [1]–[3].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Target sample: Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) with minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 for power planning. Inclusion/exclusion, missingness handling, multiplicity, and contamination controls were fixed in the preregistration.

Task generation and scope. Confirmatory items were deterministically generated from an intent_configuration_repair task family covering three abstract vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3‑node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, intent, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after at most two deterministic reseeds; the confirmatory run had zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720.

Model, sampling semantics, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model in the run configuration is "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). The client did not set an explicit temperature parameter (recorded as null). For each pair we obtained exactly one sampled initial candidate (one provider call) and presented that identical candidate to both downstream conditions (baseline and guarded). This isolates downstream guarded-stage effects by removing generation variability.

Baseline validator. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is a deterministic rule-based checker that performs vendor-CLI parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints, protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance. It outputs a binary detected/not-detected flag under the preregistered scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation and emits a validator_trace with parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation codes.

Guarded pipeline and sandboxed-emulation harness. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then executes the candidate in an automated sandboxed emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and runs normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The emulation harness records runtime observations (interface admin transitions, concurrent-interface states, MTU/VLAN application effects, observable connectivity consequences). Emulation observations are mapped to runtime-observation rules that can trigger detections not encoded in the static validator rule set. The emulation mapping is deliberately conservative: its role here is to reveal runtime-only misconfigurations that the validator might miss.

Repair policy and provider-call accounting. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model invocation per task and only after initial generation and downstream observations for the guarded condition. Provider-call auditing in the archived run reports model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. Because the initial generation was shared across both conditions, the only permissible causes of any guarded-only detection are (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not encoded as a validator violation, or (ii) the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The deterministic reconciliation artifact archived with the run reconciles episode accounting and provider-call audit fields; section Results explains how the provider-call audit entries map to episode/pair accounting under shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Provider-call audit fields: interpretation and asymmetry resolution. The archived provider_call_audit uses two nested counters relevant to readers: (a) stage_counts enumerates model-call counts by pipeline stage (e.g., shared_initial_generation, repair), and (b) condition_counts enumerates how many model calls are associated with higher-level call categories labeled by the execution adapter (keys named "shared" and "guarded"). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics a single shared initial generation produces one model call whose output is used by both baseline and guarded scoring; that call is counted under stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 720 and under condition_counts."shared" = 720 because it is the initial, shared provider invocation. The single repair-stage call that occurred is counted under stage_counts.repair = 1 and under condition_counts."guarded" = 1 because the repair invocation was associated with the guarded pipeline’s downstream decision process. Aggregating stage_counts (720 + 1 = 721) equals model_calls_used = 721. Thus the apparent asymmetry in condition_counts is explained deterministically by the shared initial generation semantics plus a single guarded repair call; the preregistered artifacts provide full audit evidence for this mapping.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inference. The paired contingency (artifact-grounded) is: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0013888889. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0041666667]. All numeric outputs are taken verbatim from the preregistered paired-binary analysis artifacts archived with the execution bundle.

Discordant-pair attribution and repair accounting. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation identify a single repair-stage invocation and the unique n10 discordant count. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single guarded-only detection is attributable either to the single recorded repair-stage invocation or to a guarded-emulation observation not codified as a validator violation. The archived reconciliation artifacts record stage_counts (shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1) and condition_counts (shared = 720, guarded = 1), which deterministically reconcile to model_calls_used = 721. The confirmatory artifacts permit an auditor to locate the singular discordant pair_id in the canonical input-results artifact and inspect per-episode validator_trace and repair transcripts to determine which downstream event produced the guarded-only detection.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-episode validator_traces in the archived scoring artifacts show parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count = 0 for the vast majority of shared_initial candidates, illustrating that the validator’s rule set matched the curated task patterns and produced a baseline success ceiling of 719/720. The single discordant event is isolated and auditable in the archived execution bundle.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The artifact-grounded evidence supports three primary, nonexclusive explanations.

1) Validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator explicitly encodes the syntactic and workflow checks exercised by the curated tasks (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). Most shared_initial candidates complied with those rules (validator traces with violation_count = 0), producing an extremely high baseline success rate (0.9986) and leaving little headroom for emulation to add detections.

2) Curated inclusion and reduced adversarial exposure. Confirmatory items were parser-validated and generated deterministically from a constrained task family; this design intentionally reduced exposure to noisy or adversarial inputs where emulation often reveals additional faults. Zero irrecoverable parser exclusions in the run confirm the constrained nature of the confirmatory sample.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. Because the initial generation was shared, any between-condition difference must originate downstream. The audit shows exactly one repair-stage invocation; that single repair maps to the single n10 discordant pair. Thus, at the scale and in the constrained distribution we tested, guarded-side interventions were nearly redundant.

Operational implications. For operator environments with a high-coverage static validator tailored to expected intent patterns and an input pipeline that enforces parser-level prevalidation, an always-on guarded sandboxed-emulation stage may produce negligible incremental detection at scale. This finding is conditional and narrow: in noisier, adversarial, multi‑vendor, or long-lived stateful regimes—where validator coverage is incomplete or emulator fidelity is materially higher—the guarded stage is likely to surface runtime semantics and side effects that static rules cannot anticipate. Practically, operators should (a) invest in validator coverage for routine low‑risk automation, (b) apply guarded sandboxing selectively for high‑risk or high‑impact changes, and (c) use adversarial/fuzzing banks to reveal validator gaps. The archived artifacts provide concrete seed traces for such adversarial test design.

Limitations tied to the archived evidence. The reported near-zero aggregate effect is specific to the preregistered task bank, the single validator implementation, the declared/requested model, and the shared_initial_candidate semantics. The study was powered to detect a 0.20 paired difference; the observed effect (~0.0014) is far below that design sensitivity and must be interpreted as a narrowly scoped null result rather than a broad generalization that guarded staging is unnecessary in all NetOps contexts.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator to the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.0013888889) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0041666667]. Provider-call auditing shows model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts indicating 720 shared initial generations and a single repair invocation; the single guarded-only detection corresponds to that downstream activity. We interpret this artifact-grounded result as arising from a validator-ceiling effect under constrained, parser-validated inputs and shared_initial_candidate semantics. Follow-up work should retest guarded staging under adversarial task banks, expanded vendor diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation; the archived execution bundle provides seed artifacts and audit trails to support such extensions.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: Autonomous post-lock research run executed under the frozen master prompt supplied to the system. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration id: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e. Initial master-prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Canonical execution manifest and full per-file provenance are archived in the run’s evidence bundle (see the canonical execution_manifest artifact in the archived bundle). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline autonomously performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic and deterministic task bank produces limited ecological diversity and produces a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) constrain generalizability across model and validator families.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream guarded-stage contributions but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains the set of discordance sources to emulation observations or repair calls.
Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the harness used; different emulation fidelity could change outcomes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) is far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime.
